keyframe_review.note: New keyframe -1865..-1802: no Cliopatria shape (Uruk sits inside the Sumerian City-States shapes, not as a state). The page names only Uruk and Durum, "a town near Uruk"; Ur, Nippur and Larsa are not under Sin-kashid on the pages. Drawn as the city and 40 km around it (my reading).

ledger.note: c. 1865 BC: Sin-kashid takes Uruk from Larsa. The infobox has his reign c. 1865-1833; "He successfully wrestled the city-state of Uruk away from the dominion of Larsa, thereby founding a 50-year dynasty"; he began as viceroy of Durum, "initially under the hegemony of the kings of Isin". The Uruk page puts the dynasty at c. 1872-1802. The larsa dossier (me-01) records no loss of Uruk at this date.

c. 1801 BC: Rim-Sin I of Larsa takes Uruk. "Around 1801 BC he sacked Uruk, sparing its inhabitants." The Sin-kashid page puts it in Rim-Sin's year 21, the year after Kisurra was annexed to Larsa (year 20), "driving out An-am's son and successor, Irdanene"; the Uruk page has Rim-Anum c. 1810-1802 and Nabi-ilishu c. 1802 as the last kings and, separately, Irdanene "defeated by Rim-Sin I in his year 14 (c. 1740 BC)", a figure that does not fit. Mirrors larsa -1801.

wars.name: Rim-Sin I's conquest of Uruk
wars.outcome: Rim-Sin I annexed Kisurra (year 20, c. 1802) and sacked Uruk (c. 1801), ending the Sin-kashid dynasty.
wars.note: The Sin-kashid page notes that the letter of Ninsatapada, Sin-kashid's daughter, may be a later Larsa scribe's invention to justify the takeover.

certainty.note: Only the city and Durum are named; the extent is the city's fields.

notes:
SCOPE. State Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names empty). The existing uruk dossier is the earlier fourth dynasty of Uruk (-2154..-2112, Utu-hengal), so this is a separate state of the same city. The larsa dossier books the loss as a gain of "Uruk (Sin-kashid dynasty)" at -1801 (mirror: dissolve here, counterpart larsa) and no loss at the foundation: the -1865 found here has no mirror in larsa (a gap-filler could add a larsa loss of Uruk at -1865 from the Sin-kashid page, which does not date Nur-Adad's reign).
PAGES. Three: Sin-kashid, Uruk, Rim-Sin I (the last shared with babylonia and larsa mirrors).
DISAGREEMENTS. Dynasty start c. 1872 (Uruk page header) vs c. 1865 (Sin-kashid and the Uruk ruler list); end c. 1802 (Uruk list, Rim-Anum then Nabi-ilishu) vs Rim-Sin I year 21 (c. 1801 by the Sin-kashid page's arithmetic from 1822) vs the Rim-Sin I page "around 1801 BC"; the Uruk page's Irdanene "year 14 (c. 1740 BC)" is inconsistent with its own table (Irdanene c. 1816-1810) and with Rim-Sin's reign (1822-1763). The Sin-kashid page says the dynasty was replaced by An-am and Irdanene after "Etēia of unknown provenance"; its lists omit Etel-pi-Marduk and Rim-Anum. The 50-year length does not fit 1865-1801 (64 years).
NOT MAPPED. Durum (Sin-kashid's earlier seat, "a town near Uruk"; the page's Der identification is doubtful) is unlocated; the Amnanum kinship and marriage to Sallurtum, daughter of Sumu-la-El of Babylon, are not territorial.
